The root of this research is unimodality by maximum displacement, as posed: the root is proved, and the proof is complete in Lean. The map shows the units the proof of the root rests on: 173 units, each a card, in 12 groups, joined by 916 lines. 183 smaller steps have no card and are folded into the lines that pass through them.

How to read the map

An arrow runs from what is used to what uses it, so the map is read from the left, where the definitions and the first results stand, towards the root. Thin lines that leave one card have one colour; where they run as one line, a dot marks each point at which one of them leaves it. Lines that cross without a dot are not connected.

  • named in the proof, or in the body of a definition
  • through folded steps (the panel names them for a selected unit)
  • mentioned in the statement
  • a proof drawn as its own card, to its statement
  • a lighter line leaves a definition
  • a statement
  • a definition
  • a proof on its own card
  • the root
  • the bar at the left of a card: accepted

The words on the cards

unit
A result or a definition that one would name when saying how the proof goes. Every card is a unit.
step
A result that lives inside one proof. A step has no card; it is folded into the lines that pass through it.
root
The proposition the research set out to settle.
statement
A proposition stated in Lean. Its card says how its proof stands.
definition
A definition of the Lean library.
inductive type
A type of the Lean library that is given by its constructors.
proof
A proof of a statement, drawn as a card of its own. The declaration of the statement itself carries no proof.
proof on a separate card
The declaration of this statement carries no proof. Its proof is the card that the heavy line comes from.
accepted
Review found the proof correct and accepted it.
settled
One of its proofs is accepted, and every statement that proof names is settled in the same way.
formal
One of its proofs is complete in Lean: it rests on nothing but the allowed axioms, with no gap below it.
